name: Nicotine

card.summary: The stimulant and addictive alkaloid in tobacco and pouches, used by some in appearance communities as an appetite suppressant; no trials test it for leanness, and its documented harms are well established.
card.aka: Nicotine pouches (Zyn, Velo), nicotine gum, patch, vape
card.note: Highly addictive; raises heart rate and blood pressure. Approved nicotine products are labelled for smoking cessation, not weight loss.

quick.overview:
Nicotine is the main psychoactive alkaloid in tobacco. It is sold in cigarettes, vapes, oral pouches, gum, lozenges and patches. Regulated nicotine replacement products are marketed to reduce withdrawal and craving in people quitting smoking.

In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a way to suppress appetite and 'leanmaxx', and as a focus aid. Other posters describe it as harmful to looks, citing sleep, skin, teeth, hair and anxiety complaints. The cessation literature is large; the evidence for any appearance or fat-loss use specifically is thin.
quick.mechanism: Nicotine activates nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, prompting release of dopamine and other neurotransmitters. Forum posts attribute appetite suppression and higher energy expenditure to this action; those posts cite older physiological studies that are not evaluated in this article's sources.
quick.risks: Nicotine is addictive, raises heart rate and blood pressure, and the FDA-listed labels for nicotine gum caution people with heart disease and pregnant users. E-cigarettes and pouches have been studied for oral and other effects, with long-term data still accumulating. Forum users report insomnia, anxiety, palpitations and dependence.

lead: Nicotine is a plant alkaloid found chiefly in the tobacco plant and is the principal addictive component of tobacco products. It acts on nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in the nervous system and increases release of dopamine and other neurotransmitters [3][10]. It was first isolated from tobacco in 1828 by the German chemists Wilhelm Heinrich Posselt and Karl Ludwig Reimann [1][34].

People in appearance communities use it for leanness. Nicotine reduces hunger and food intake and raises energy expenditure according to the pharmacology literature summarised on Wikipedia, and forum users cite this when they use gum, vapes and especially oral pouches during a cut to stay lean enough to show facial and muscular definition [22][28][34]. Others use it as a focus aid. The pouch category grew from roughly 292 million units sold worldwide in 2018 to about 20.1 billion in 2023, with the brand Zyn holding more than 70 percent of the market [35].

Regulated nicotine products such as gum, lozenges and patches are used in nicotine replacement therapy to ease withdrawal during smoking cessation [5][6][8]. The US label for nicotine polacrilex gum states that it reduces withdrawal symptoms, including craving, associated with quitting smoking, and warns that nicotine can raise heart rate and blood pressure [2].

Other community members argue that nicotine harms appearance, and some report quitting as improving it [23][30]. No clinical study found for this article has tested nicotine as an appearance or fat-loss intervention in people who do not smoke.

paras: Nicotine replacement therapy delivers nicotine in gum, patches, nasal spray, inhalers and lozenges to reduce the urge to smoke and withdrawal symptoms [6]. A 1990 randomized trial of a transdermal patch in highly dependent smokers found higher abstinence than placebo, along with reduced withdrawal symptoms such as negative affect [8]. Cochrane reviews have assessed NRT and electronic cigarettes as smoking-cessation aids [4][6].
Nicotine has also been studied in other research settings, for example attention and cognition in people with schizophrenia, and a small pilot in sarcoidosis [9][18].

Forum users describe nicotine, particularly pouches and gum, as an appetite suppressant and a way to stay lean during a diet [22][28][21]. One widely read looksmax.org thread presents nicotine as a stimulant for fat loss and lists older physiological studies in support [22]. The chain proposed is nicotine, to reduced hunger and a modest rise in energy expenditure, to a calorie deficit, to lower body fat and a leaner face and physique.

Pharmacology references describe the underlying effect: nicotine reduces hunger and food intake and increases energy expenditure, most research finds it reduces body weight, and the proposed mechanism involves alpha3-beta4 receptors on POMC neurons in the melanocortin system [34]. This matches the observation that people who quit smoking commonly gain weight, which forum posters cite as evidence of the appetite effect [22]. No randomized trial identified for this article tests nicotine for fat loss, facial leanness or other appearance outcomes.

subs.h: Tobacco and the isolation of nicotine
paras: Tobacco reached Europe in the early 1530s, brought by Spanish explorers. In 1560 the French ambassador in Portugal, Jean Nicot de Villemain, sent tobacco and seeds to Paris and promoted its medicinal use; the genus Nicotiana is named after him [34]. Posselt and Reimann isolated nicotine in 1828, believing it a poison; Louis Melsens described its empirical formula in 1843, Adolf Pinner and Richard Wolffenstein determined its structure in 1893, and Ame Pictet and A. Rotschy first synthesised it in 1904 [34].

Tobacco was also used as an insecticide, with use peaking after World War II at over 2,500 tons worldwide and falling below 200 tons by the 1980s; nicotine insecticides were banned in the US in 2014 [34].

Nicotine replacement therapy developed in the late twentieth century as gum, patches, lozenges, nasal sprays and inhalers; a 1990 randomized trial reported higher abstinence with a transdermal patch than placebo [8]. The first pouch product came from the startup Niconovum in the early 2000s, registered in 2008 as a medicinal replacement product (Zonnic, 2 mg); RJ Reynolds bought the company in 2009 and tobacco firms, especially Swedish Match, then entered the category, building on Sweden's snus tradition [35].

Sweden's Act on Tobacco-Free Nicotine Products took effect on 1 August 2022 [35]. In 2018 Norway's health directorate forced BAT to pull its Epok pouch, which returned days later with a small amount of tobacco so that it qualified as snus [35]. In January 2025 the US FDA authorised 20 Zyn products through its premarket tobacco application pathway, finding lower exposure to certain harmful chemicals than cigarettes but still health risks and adult-only use [35].

Nicotine binds nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, ligand-gated ion channels found throughout the central and peripheral nervous system [10]. In rat experiments, nicotine and other drugs that humans misuse increased extracellular dopamine in the nucleus accumbens, a finding frequently cited in discussions of reward and dependence [3].

Nicotine is an agonist at most nicotinic receptors but an antagonist at the alpha9 and alpha10 subunits; it releases dopamine in the mesolimbic pathway and epinephrine from the adrenal medulla, and its effect shifts from stimulant to sedative as dose rises, a pattern called Nesbitt's paradox, first described in 1969 [34].

Studies have compared the pharmacokinetics of nicotine patches and the nicotine delivered by vaping pods [11][12]. Oral nicotine pouches have been the subject of a recent public health review describing their rising popularity [13].

Inhaled nicotine reaches the brain within 10 to 20 seconds. Bioavailability is about 80 to 90 percent by inhalation, 68 to 100 percent transdermally, 60 to 80 percent intranasally and about 65 percent sublingually; metabolism is mainly hepatic via CYP2A6, and the elimination half-life is about two hours, while the metabolite cotinine lasts roughly 16 to 20 hours [34].

Human trials of nicotine concern smoking cessation, product pharmacokinetics, cognition and physiology rather than appearance. A Cochrane review examines nicotine replacement for long-term cessation [6], and another Cochrane living review examines e-cigarettes for cessation [4]. Randomized trials have also tested patches, nasal spray and lozenges for bioequivalence, attention and oral mucosal effects [17][19][20].

A 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis found that, compared with cigarette smokers, e-cigarette users had a lower chance of bleeding on probing and less plaque, probing depth and attachment loss, while the authors noted comparisons with non-smokers as well [14]. This concerns periodontal health, not appearance directly.

A 2023 meta-analysis of social media use and health risk behaviours in adolescents included tobacco and nicotine vaping among the outcomes; it did not study nicotine's effect on looks [15]. No study found tests whether nicotine reduces body fat in people without a dependence indication, alters facial appearance, hair, collagen or testosterone.

The US label for nicotine polacrilex gum advises people with heart disease, recent heart attack, irregular heartbeat or uncontrolled high blood pressure to ask a doctor before use because nicotine can raise heart rate and blood pressure. It advises pregnant or breast-feeding people to use it only on a health care provider's advice [2].

Wikipedia's nicotine article reports that consumer doses pose little acute hazard to adults, that high doses can cause nausea, vomiting, slow heart rate, seizures and death, that nicotine transiently raises blood pressure, that it reduces REM and slow-wave sleep in a dose-dependent way, that dependence can develop within days, and that withdrawal peaks within one to three days and can last several weeks. It is not classed as a carcinogen by IARC or the US Surgeon General but is a possible teratogen, and use in pregnancy is not considered safe [34].
Nicotine is described across pharmacological literature as dependence-forming, and instruments such as the Fagerström Test have been developed to measure nicotine dependence [16].

Forum users report their own experiences. One poster on looksmax.org attributed insomnia, palpitations, brain fog, hair loss and other symptoms to pouches [23]; other threads discuss anxiety, facial bloating and balding [26][25][32]. These are individual reports and have not been verified in controlled studies. Other users describe feeling better after quitting [30].

Global pouch sales rose from an estimated 292 million units in 2018 to 20.1 billion in 2023, about 85 percent of them in the US, with Zyn holding over 70 percent of the global market [35]. Flavours and discreet use have been cited as appealing to young adults, including never-smokers; a 2025 UK report found about 1.2 percent of 11 to 18 year olds were current users [35]. Reviews describe pouches as exposing users to substantially fewer tobacco toxicants than cigarettes, while noting that independent testing is limited, many studies are industry-funded and long-term effects are uncertain [35][13].

A 2024 independent trial cited by Wikipedia found that 30 mg pouches produced plasma nicotine levels about twice those of cigarettes, with increased heart rate and arterial stiffness [35]. Accidental ingestion by children under six rose about 763 percent between 2020 and 2023, and in September 2025 the FDA urged manufacturers to use child-resistant packaging [35].

The US FDA regulates nicotine as a tobacco product under the 2009 Family Smoking Prevention and Tobacco Control Act, and a March 2022 law extended that to nicotine from any source, including synthetic; in January 2025 the agency proposed capping nicotine in cigarettes at 0.7 mg per gram of tobacco [34]. Nicotine is over-the-counter and prescription in the US, general-sales-list in the UK and Schedule 7 in Australia [34]. Minimum purchase age is 21 federally in the US and 18 in the EU and UK [34].

Pouches are lightly regulated in the EU and are sold in UK supermarkets outside tobacco and medicines law, though the UK Tobacco and Vapes Bill introduced in 2024 would ban sales to under-18s [35]. Canada restricted Zonnic to pharmacies in August 2024, Finland banned distance sales from 1 August 2025, Spain added an excise tax of 0.10 euro per gram from April 2025, and France planned a ban from 1 April 2026 [35].

Threads such as 'Nicotine for fatloss guide' and 'nicotine for appetite suppression' present nicotine as a tool for leanness and focus, often citing physiological studies on energy expenditure and appetite [22][28]. Some posters argue that pouches are preferable to smoking or vaping because of smell and other considerations [22].

Others dispute this. A thread titled 'Nicotine pouches will destroy you' lists symptoms the author attributes to heavy use [23], and other threads ask whether pouches affect looks [29]. Posts on T Nation mention nicotine in passing, including one user's belief that tobacco use affected gynecomastia, which is the poster's own speculation [33].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org nicotine appears both as a leanmaxxing stimulant and as a feared 'looksmin' factor, with pouches now the most discussed form [22][23][29].

claims.claim: Nicotine suppresses appetite and speeds up fat loss.
claims.believers: Users say it blunts hunger and raises metabolism during a cut, citing older studies on energy expenditure and weight after quitting [22][28].
claims.experts: Reviews of nicotine products focus on smoking cessation; none of the published literature test nicotine as a fat-loss intervention in people without dependence.

claims.believers: Posters list improved attention and working memory through nicotinic receptors [21].
claims.experts: Randomized studies have examined nicotine's effects on attention in specific populations such as people with schizophrenia [9].

claims.claim: Nicotine raises testosterone or blocks its conversion to estrogen.
claims.believers: Thread titles assert increases of around 15 percent or that nicotine stops conversion to estrogen [24][27], and one T Nation user calls it a 'mild AI' [33].
claims.experts: No study in the published literature tests these claims.

claims.claim: Nicotine pouches harm looks (hair, skin, teeth, sleep).
claims.believers: Posters attribute hair loss, collagen loss, insomnia and dental problems to pouches [23][32].
claims.experts: Research on oral and periodontal outcomes compares cigarettes and e-cigarettes rather than pouches [14]; hair and collagen outcomes are not covered in the published literature.

claims.claim: Nicotine is addictive and can cause anxiety and unease.
claims.believers: Users report dependence, anxiety and switching to energy drinks after quitting [26][31].
claims.experts: Nicotine is characterised as the addictive component of tobacco, and dependence scales exist; labels list cardiovascular cautions [2][16].

claims.claim: Pouches are a cleaner alternative to smoking or vaping for staying lean.
claims.believers: One thread argues pouches are preferable to smoking or vaping because of smell and other practicalities [22].
claims.experts: Reviews report lower exposure to tobacco toxicants than cigarettes but limited independent testing and uncertain long-term effects; a 2024 trial found some strengths raised heart rate and arterial stiffness [35][13].

claims.claim: Nicotine suppresses appetite, so quitting causes weight gain.
claims.believers: Posters cite post-quitting weight gain as proof that nicotine keeps weight down [22].
claims.experts: Pharmacology references report reduced hunger, reduced food intake and higher energy expenditure with nicotine, and most research finds lower body weight [34].
